author: "Anthony Morciglio"

output: html_document

## Introduction

This R Markdown file demonstrates the visualization of continuous and differentiable functions.  
We plot two main examples:
1. The **absolute value function**, which is continuous everywhere but not differentiable at \( x = 0 \).  
2. A **smooth polynomial function**, \( f(x) = x^3 - 3x + 1 \), which is both continuous and differentiable everywhere.

The plots help illustrate how differentiability implies continuity, but continuity alone does not guarantee differentiability.

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Load necessary package
library(ggplot2)

# Create a sequence of x values
x <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 400)

# Define the functions
f_continuous <- abs(x)                  # Continuous but not differentiable
f_differentiable <- x^2                 # Continuous and differentiable

# Combine into a data frame
df <- data.frame(
  x = x,
  Continuous = f_continuous,
  Differentiable = f_differentiable
)

# Melt data for ggplot
library(reshape2)
df_long <- melt(df, id.vars = "x", variable.name = "Function", value.name = "y")

# Plot both functions
ggplot(df_long, aes(x = x, y = y, color = Function)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.2, y = 2.5, label = "Non-differentiable point", hjust = 0, size = 4) +
  labs(title = "Continuous vs Differentiable Functions",
       x = "x",
       y = "f(x)",
       caption = "The absolute value function is continuous but not differentiable at x = 0.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```
